rendered:
The document doesn't report any results for the D-HGNR-based probe (BA@D-HGNRs) on clinical sepsis serum samples. Only the L-form probe was tested on those samples.

What the paper does show for the D-form probe:
- It was compared with the L-form probe in a test of whether the probe's handedness matters. The L- and D-form probes gave CD signals of opposite sign, but the response sizes stayed closely comparable[1] ([2]Fig. 2[3]). The authors concluded that recognition is largely independent of handedness, so BA@L-HGNRs were employed as the probe for subsequent work.[4]
- Its only other mention: in the aqueous multi-bacteria discrimination test, BA@D-HGNRs also effectively validates this phenomenon[5], meaning the clusters don't overlap. This result is in a supplementary figure.

For the clinical sepsis serum (patients with E. coli infection, patients with E. faecium infection, and healthy controls), only the L-form probe was used. Its LDA plot showed well-resolved, non-overlapping clusters for the three tested serum groups[6], which the authors credit to the BA@L-HGNRs probe[7] (Fig. 5[8]).

So how the D-form probe would do on sepsis serum isn't shown in the document.
